title: Artists who recorded his songs; Bernstein; minimizing his piano playing
summary: Rasch lists artists who recorded his songs, notes over 200 songs, and says he plays down his piano but made noodling tapes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Some of J. C.'s songs were recorded by the following people: Red Allen, Count Basie, Connie Boswell, Billy Butterfield, Bing Crosby, Duke Ellington, Ella Fitzgerald, Al Hibbler, Earl Hines, Billie Holiday, Claude Hopkins, James P. Johnson,

Pete Kelly, Dean Kincaid, Freddie Martin, Don Redmond, Della Reese, Bessie Smith -- we're going alphabetically, as you can see -- Fats Waller, Kaye Stark, Dinah Washington, Ethel Waters, Josh White, Paul Young, Paul Whiteman, Lester Young and others.

He has written over 200 songs. I don't know exactly how many are recorded. I think the recording that he's especially proud of is Leonard Bernstein's introduction to music in which he refers to his "Empty Bed Blues" and calls it the greatest blues song ever written. And J. C. is really thrilled with that honor from Leonard Bernstein, and he says, "That's pretty highbrow, isn't it."

J. C. minimizes his own piano playing. His composing is the thing that he's really proud of. But those of us who have sat around and listened to him play the piano feel very, very privileged. He made some tapes of his "Noodling" where he just sits down and composes. It's really an improvisational thing and it's gorgeous. He has this tape at his home in (Wurtzboro), New York, and as soon as he gets out of the hospital again, gets up here, which he does not anticipate until the spring. However, the Smithsonian will get it. He has promised it for them and I know that you'll have it.
